metadata.summary: Mensur Suljovic's crowd incitement during his match against Ross Smith and his alleged sexist comments in his on-stage interview regarding the incident have been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority.
metadata.content: Mensur Suljovic referred to darts regulator for inciting jeers against Ross Smith and alleged sexist comments as Austrian issues apology | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mensur Suljovic referred to darts regulator for inciting jeers against Ross Smith and alleged sexist comments as Austrian issues apology Mensur Suljovic has been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority for his incitement of jeers against Ross Smith in their clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy; he has also been referred over his alleged sexist comments in an interview about the incident; the Austrian has issued an apology Monday 12 October 2026 18:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mensur Suljovic encouraged the crowd to boo Ross Smith as he stepped up to take his match-winning darts - before then winning the match himself (credit - PDC) Mensur Suljovic's crowd incitement during his match against Ross Smith and his alleged sexist comments in his on-stage interview regarding the incident have been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority. The Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in their third-round clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy on Sunday afternoon. He was later asked about the incident in an on-stage interview and used an allegedly sexist comment to describe how Smith reacted. metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton has posted on social media to reiterate has apology to Ferrari after a "painful lesson" at the Singapore Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver releases statement on Instagram after 'painful lesson' at Singapore GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver releases statement on Instagram after 'painful lesson' at Singapore GP Lewis Hamilton took to social media to apologise to Ferrari once again after his strategy call saw him drop out of the podium positions at the Singapore Grand Prix; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Monday 12 October 2026 15:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chadhok dissects Lewis Hamilton's Singapore GP race Lewis Hamilton has posted on social media to reiterate has apology to Ferrari after a "painful lesson" at the Singapore Grand Prix. Hamilton overrode Ferrari's strategy while on course for a podium finish by opting not to pit for fresh tyres during a Virtual Safety Car (VSC) period, leaving him vulnerable in the closing stages of the race. He was overtaken by Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, who did pit when the VSC came out, and was subsequently passed by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, plus McLaren duo Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri as he dropped to sixth. messages.text: Bashir and Pope given new England contracts

metadata.summary: England have renewed the central contracts of Ollie Pope and Shoaib Bashir for one year despite the duo dropping out of the Test XI but Zak Crawley's expiring deal has not been extended.
metadata.content: England cricket central contracts: Shoaib Bashir, Ollie Pope deals renewed as Henry Crocombe, Jordan Cox sign for two years | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England cricket central contracts: Shoaib Bashir, Ollie Pope deals renewed as Henry Crocombe, Jordan Cox sign for two years Ben Stokes and Mark Wood's deals finish after international retirements; Zak Crawley's not renewed; 39 players contracted with 11 deals running until 2028, including Sonny Baker, who is upgraded to two-year deal; England add ex-South Africa international Eric Simons to Test coaching staff Monday 12 October 2026 14:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England managing director Rob Key explains why off-spinner Shoaib Bashir has been awarded a new central contract England have renewed the central contracts of Ollie Pope and Shoaib Bashir for one year despite the duo dropping out of the Test XI but Zak Crawley's expiring deal has not been extended. A total of 39 players are now under contract with Ollie Robinson, uncapped fellow seamer Henry Crocombe and Crawley's replacement as opener in the Test side, Emilio Gay , among eight previously uncontracted players to be rewarded with full deals. They join batters Jordan Cox, Dan Lawrence and Tom Banton and pacemen Sam Cook and Matthew Fisher , with all but Robinson - who had a deal in 2022 and 2023 - handed contracts for the first time.
